title: Going, coming, returning
japaneseTitle: みんなの日本語 第5課
summary: Build a movement sentence by attaching destination, transport, companion, and time to 行きます・来ます・帰ります.
sourceFiles: みんなの日本語　第5課.pdf
takeaways: に or へ points toward the destination.
で marks transport; と marks a companion.
Question word + も + negative gives “nowhere/no one/nothing.”

grammar.title: Choose the destination
grammar.pattern: Place に／へ 行きます
grammar.summary: に treats the place as a target. へ emphasizes direction toward it. At this level, both usually translate as “to.”

examples.english: I will go to Hakone on the weekend.
I will return to my country next month.

grammar.title: Add transport and company
grammar.summary: で shows the means used for movement. と joins the person who accompanies you.

examples.english: I go to Osaka by bullet train.
I went to Kyoto with my family.

grammar.caution: Walking takes 歩いて, not a transport noun + で. Learn it as a fixed answer for now.

grammar.title: Turn a question word into “none”
grammar.summary: Combine a question word with も and a negative predicate to mean no one, nothing, nowhere, or never.

examples.english: I did not go with anyone.

grammar.caution: Keep the negative ending. Without it, the meaning does not become “none.”

recall.prompt: Which particle marks the vehicle used?
What is the nuance difference between destination に and へ?
recall.answer: に targets the endpoint; へ emphasizes direction toward it.

recall.prompt: How do you say “I did not go anywhere”?
recall.answer: どこにも行きませんでした。
